chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ra'ab, from Abu Ubayda al-Hadda', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When one of you recites the Sajdah verse from the decisive (obligatory) ones, let him say in his prostration: 'I have prostrated to You as an act of worship and servitude, not being too arrogant to worship You, nor too proud, nor too exalted, but I am a humble servant, fearful, seeking refuge.'
ai.seo_question: What should be said during prostration when reciting an obligatory Quranic verse?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi outlines the specific supplication for the sajdat al-tilawah (prostration of recitation) of the decisive verses, emphasizing a posture of humble servitude ('abd dhaleel) and fear ('akhif) before Allah. It serves as a practical guide for believers to internalize the spiritual state of humility during worship, contrasting true submission with the arrogance of the proud. This practice is rooted in the Shia tradition of enhancing the quality of prayer through precise verbal and physical acts of devotion.
